"""
Shared constants and helpers of the kanban storage.

The kanban catalogue lives in ``<codx_path>/tasks`` and is stored in **v2
format** (see :mod:`codx.junior.kanban.store`):

```
.codx/tasks/
  index.json                       { version: 2, boards: [ {id,title,type,parent_id,folder,order} ], tags }
  boards/<board_id>/board.json     { id,title,description,type,parent_id,folder,columns:[{id,title,color,folder,order}] }
  <folder>/<column_folder>/<slug>.<chat_id>.json
```

``folder`` is **immutable**: it is the name of the directory that holds the
board/column chats. ``title`` is only a label, so renaming a board or a column
changes nothing on disk and no task has to be rewritten.

This module must stay dependency free (no imports from the rest of codx-junior)
because both the store and the migration import it.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import os
import re

# Bumped whenever the on-disk layout changes in a breaking way.
STORE_VERSION = 2

# Version reported by the legacy (v1) single-file layout.
LEGACY_VERSION = 0.1

INDEX_FILE = "index.json"
BOARDS_DIR = "boards"
BOARD_FILE = "board.json"
LEGACY_FILE = "kanban.json"
BACKUP_FILE = "kanban.v1.backup.json"
LOCK_FILE = ".kanban.lock"

DEFAULT_BOARD = "kanban"
DEFAULT_COLUMN = "tasks"
BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN = "kanban"
BOARD_TYPE_SPRINT = "sprint"

# Characters that can never appear in a directory name used as a folder.
_INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS = re.compile(r'[/\\\x00-\x1f]')


def safe_folder(name: str, default: str = "board") -> str:
    """
    Convert a board/column *title* into a directory name.

    The original case and spaces are preserved on purpose: existing projects
    already have folders such as ``To do`` or ``tasks``, and changing them would
    orphan every stored chat.

    Args:
        name: Board or column title.
        default: Value used when the title has no usable characters.

    Returns:
        A path separator free folder name.

    Example:
        >>> safe_folder("To do")
        'To do'
        >>> safe_folder("api/ui")
        'api-ui'
    """
    folder = _INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS.sub("-", str(name or "")).strip()
    folder = folder.strip(".").strip()
    return folder or default


def is_store_file(file_path: str) -> bool:
    """
    Tell whether *file_path* is part of the storage itself (not a chat).

    ``.codx/tasks`` holds both the chats and the catalogue, so any code that
    walks the tree for chats must skip ``index.json``, the legacy
    ``kanban.json`` and everything under ``boards/``.

    Args:
        file_path: Absolute or relative file path.

    Returns:
        True when the path belongs to the kanban storage.
    """
    base = os.path.basename(file_path)
    if base in (INDEX_FILE, LEGACY_FILE, BACKUP_FILE, LOCK_FILE):
        return True
    parts = os.path.normpath(file_path).split(os.sep)
    return BOARDS_DIR in parts

"""
Migrate the kanban catalogue from the single ``tasks/kanban.json`` file (v1)
to the split layout (v2): ``tasks/index.json`` + ``tasks/boards/<id>/board.json``.

Why the split
-------------
v1 is read‑modify‑write over one file with no lock, and it is written by the UI
*and* by the tools. Two writers can silently drop a board. v2 keeps one small
file per board plus a light index, so a write touches a single board.

Guarantees of this migration
----------------------------
* **Idempotent**: a board id is derived from the board name
  (``uuid5``), so re-running produces the same ids and files.
* **Non destructive**: the legacy file is copied to
  ``kanban.v1.backup.json`` *before* anything is written, and it is only removed
  after every board file has been written and verified.
* **Folder preserving**: the folder of every board and column is the name that
  is already used on disk, so no chat has to be moved.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import uuid
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from codx.junior.kanban.model import (
    BACKUP_FILE,
    BOARD_FILE,
    BOARDS_DIR,
    BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN,
    BOARD_TYPE_SPRINT,
    INDEX_FILE,
    LEGACY_FILE,
    LEGACY_VERSION,
    STORE_VERSION,
    safe_folder,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Namespace used to derive a STABLE board id from its name.
_ID_NAMESPACE = uuid.UUID("6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00c04fc964ff")


def stable_board_id(tasks_path: str, name: str) -> str:
    """
    Return the deterministic id of a board.

    Using ``uuid5`` keeps the migration idempotent: migrating twice, or loading
    a project whose index was lost, regenerates the same ids instead of
    duplicating the boards.

    Args:
        tasks_path: Absolute ``tasks`` folder (scopes the id to the project).
        name: Board name/title.

    Returns:
        A UUID string.
    """
    return str(uuid.uuid5(_ID_NAMESPACE, f"{tasks_path}::{name}"))


def _read_json(file_path: str) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Read a JSON file, returning None when it is missing or unreadable."""
    if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
        return None
    try:
        with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            data = json.loads(handle.read())
        return data if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    except (OSError, ValueError) as ex:
        logger.warning("kanban migration: cannot read '%s': %s", file_path, ex)
        return None


def _write_json(file_path: str, data: dict) -> None:
    """Write JSON atomically (temporary file + ``os.replace``)."""
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_path), exist_ok=True)
    tmp_path = f"{file_path}.tmp"
    with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
    os.replace(tmp_path, file_path)


def _board_type(entry: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Return the canonical board type of a legacy entry."""
    board_type = str(entry.get("type") or "").strip().lower()
    if board_type in (BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN, BOARD_TYPE_SPRINT):
        return board_type
    return BOARD_TYPE_SPRINT if entry.get("sprint") else BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN


def _columns(entry: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Normalize the columns of a legacy board entry.

    Legacy files store columns either as ``{"<title>": {...}}`` or as a list of
    ``{"title": ...}`` dicts (and, in the oldest ones, as plain strings).
    """
    raw = entry.get("columns")
    if isinstance(raw, dict):
        items = [{"title": name, **(value if isinstance(value, dict) else {})}
                 for name, value in raw.items()]
    elif isinstance(raw, list):
        items = raw
    else:
        items = []

    columns: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for order, column in enumerate(items):
        if isinstance(column, str):
            column = {"title": column}
        if not isinstance(column, dict):
            continue
        title = (column.get("title") or column.get("name") or "").strip()
        if not title:
            continue
        columns.append({
            "id": column.get("id") or str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "title": title,
            "color": column.get("color") or "",
            # Existing chats live in a directory named after the column.
            "folder": column.get("folder") or safe_folder(title, default="tasks"),
            "order": column.get("order") if column.get("order") is not None else order,
        })
    return columns


def _boards(legacy: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return a normalized ``[(name, entry), ...]`` list from a legacy payload."""
    raw = legacy.get("boards")
    if isinstance(raw, dict):
        return [(str(name), entry if isinstance(entry, dict) else {})
                for name, entry in raw.items()]
    if isinstance(raw, list):
        return [
            (str(entry.get("title") or entry.get("name") or entry.get("id") or ""),
             entry)
            for entry in raw
            if isinstance(entry, dict)
        ]
    return []


def migrate_kanban_v1_to_v2(tasks_path: str, dry_run: bool = False) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Convert ``tasks/kanban.json`` into the v2 layout.

    Args:
        tasks_path: Absolute path of the project's ``tasks`` folder.
        dry_run: Compute the result without writing anything (used by tests and
            by the migration report).

    Returns:
        A summary dict: ``{"migrated", "boards", "index_file", "backup_file"}``.

    Example:
        >>> migrate_kanban_v1_to_v2("/proj/.codx/tasks")["boards"]
        3
    """
    tasks_path = str(tasks_path)
    legacy_path = os.path.join(tasks_path, LEGACY_FILE)
    index_path = os.path.join(tasks_path, INDEX_FILE)
    backup_path = os.path.join(tasks_path, BACKUP_FILE)

    summary = {
        "migrated": False,
        "boards": 0,
        "index_file": index_path,
        "backup_file": backup_path,
    }

    if os.path.isfile(index_path):
        logger.info("kanban migration: already migrated (%s exists)", index_path)
        return summary

    legacy = _read_json(legacy_path)
    if legacy is None:
        logger.info("kanban migration: no legacy file at %s, nothing to do", legacy_path)
        return summary

    # v1 files without a version envelope stored the boards at the root level.
    if not legacy.get("version"):
        legacy = {"version": LEGACY_VERSION, "boards": legacy, "tags": {}}

    entries: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    board_files: List[tuple] = []

    for order, (name, entry) in enumerate(_boards(legacy)):
        title = (entry.get("title") or name or "").strip() or f"board-{order}"
        board_id = stable_board_id(tasks_path, title)
        folder = entry.get("folder") or safe_folder(title)
        board = {
            **entry,
            "id": board_id,
            "title": title,
            "description": entry.get("description") or "",
            "type": _board_type(entry),
            "parent_id": entry.get("parent_id"),
            # The folder already holds the tasks: never move it here.
            "folder": folder,
            "columns": _columns(entry),
            "order": order,
        }
        entries.append({
            "id": board_id,
            "title": title,
            "type": board["type"],
            "parent_id": board.get("parent_id"),
            "folder": folder,
            "order": order,
        })
        board_files.append((os.path.join(tasks_path, BOARDS_DIR, board_id, BOARD_FILE), board))

    summary["boards"] = len(entries)

    if dry_run:
        summary["migrated"] = True
        return summary

    # Back up the legacy file BEFORE writing anything.
    try:
        shutil.copy2(legacy_path, backup_path)
    except OSError as ex:
        logger.error("kanban migration: cannot back up '%s': %s", legacy_path, ex)
        return summary

    for file_path, board in board_files:
        _write_json(file_path, board)

    _write_json(index_path, {
        "version": STORE_VERSION,
        "boards": entries,
        "tags": legacy.get("tags") or {},
    })

    written = sum(
        1 for file_path, _ in board_files if os.path.isfile(file_path)
    )
    if written != len(board_files):
        logger.error(
            "kanban migration: %d of %d board files written, keeping the legacy "
            "file in place",
            written,
            len(board_files),
        )
        return summary

    try:
        os.remove(legacy_path)
    except OSError as ex:
        logger.warning("kanban migration: cannot remove '%s': %s", legacy_path, ex)

    summary["migrated"] = True
    logger.info(
        "kanban migration: %d board(s) migrated (%s -> %s)",
        len(entries),
        legacy_path,
        index_path,
    )
    return summary

"""
Kanban storage v2: one file per board, atomic writes, cross-process lock.

Problem solved
--------------
v1 kept every board of a project in a single ``tasks/kanban.json`` written with
read‑modify‑write and no lock, by the UI *and* by the tools. A concurrent write
dropped boards. v2 keeps:

* ``tasks/index.json`` - the board list (id, title, type, parent, folder, order)
  plus the project tags,
* ``tasks/boards/<board_id>/board.json`` - the full definition of one board
  (description, columns, parents...).

Both are written atomically (``tmp`` + ``os.replace``) while holding a project
level ``fcntl`` lock, so the API process and the background process can write
the same catalogue without losing data.

Identity
--------
``id`` and ``folder`` are immutable. ``title`` is a label: renaming a board or a
column changes nothing on disk, so **no task is moved or rewritten**.

Compatibility
-------------
:meth:`KanbanStore.load` returns the *assembled* legacy shape::

    {"version": 2, "boards": {"<title>": {...}}, "tags": {...}}

so ``GET /api/kanban`` and the Vue client keep working unchanged, and
``POST /api/kanban`` (the whole assembled document) is diffed against the index
by :meth:`KanbanStore.save`.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import logging
import os
import shutil
import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List, Optional, Tuple

try:  # POSIX only; the container always has it.
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non POSIX fallback
    fcntl = None

from codx.junior.kanban.model import (
    BACKUP_FILE,
    BOARD_FILE,
    BOARDS_DIR,
    BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN,
    DEFAULT_BOARD,
    DEFAULT_COLUMN,
    INDEX_FILE,
    LEGACY_FILE,
    LOCK_FILE,
    STORE_VERSION,
    safe_folder,
)
from codx.junior.migrations.kanban_v1_to_v2 import migrate_kanban_v1_to_v2

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class KanbanStore:
    """
    Persistence of the kanban catalogue (boards, sprints and columns).

    Attributes:
        tasks_path: Absolute ``<codx_path>/tasks`` folder.
    """

    def __init__(self, tasks_path: str) -> None:
        """
        Args:
            tasks_path: Absolute path of the project's ``tasks`` folder.
        """
        self.tasks_path = str(tasks_path)
        self.boards_path = os.path.join(self.tasks_path, BOARDS_DIR)
        self._cache_key: Optional[Tuple[str, Optional[float]]] = None
        self._cache: Optional[Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]] = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Paths
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _path(self, *parts: str) -> str:
        """Join *parts* onto the tasks folder."""
        return os.path.join(self.tasks_path, *parts)

    def _index_file(self) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the index file."""
        return self._path(INDEX_FILE)

    def _board_file(self, board_id: Optional[str]) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the definition file of *board_id*."""
        return self._path(BOARDS_DIR, str(board_id or ""), BOARD_FILE)

    def _board_dir(self, board_id: Optional[str]) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the folder that holds the definition of *board_id*."""
        return self._path(BOARDS_DIR, str(board_id or ""))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Low level IO
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _read_json(file_path: str) -> Optional[dict]:
        """Read a JSON object, returning None when missing or unreadable."""
        if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
            return None
        try:
            with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                data = json.loads(handle.read())
            return data if isinstance(data, dict) else None
        except (OSError, ValueError) as ex:
            logger.warning("kanban: cannot read '%s': %s", file_path, ex)
            return None

    @staticmethod
    def _write_json(file_path: str, data: dict) -> None:
        """Write *data* atomically so a crash never leaves a half written file."""
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_path), exist_ok=True)
        tmp_path = f"{file_path}.tmp"
        with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
        os.replace(tmp_path, file_path)

    @contextmanager
    def locked(self) -> Iterator[None]:
        """
        Hold the project wide kanban lock.

        The lock file is opened in append mode and ``flock``ed exclusively: it
        serialises every writer **across processes** (the API process and the
        background process), which is what makes concurrent board edits safe.
        On platforms without ``fcntl`` the context manager degrades to a no-op
        instead of failing.
        """
        lock_file = self._path(LOCK_FILE)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(lock_file) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        handle = open(lock_file, "a+", encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            if fcntl is not None:
                fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            yield
        finally:
            try:
                if fcntl is not None:
                    fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            finally:
                handle.close()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Migration
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def migrate_if_needed(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Ensure the project uses the v2 layout.

        Returns:
            The migration summary (``{"migrated": False, ...}`` when there was
            nothing to do).
        """
        if os.path.isfile(self._index_file()):
            return {"migrated": False, "boards": 0}
        try:
            return migrate_kanban_v1_to_v2(tasks_path=self.tasks_path)
        except Exception as ex:  # a broken catalogue must never break a chat
            logger.exception("kanban: migration failed for '%s': %s", self.tasks_path, ex)
            return {"migrated": False, "boards": 0}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reading
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _catalogue(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Return the boards indexed by **lowercase title**, with a short lived cache.

        The cache is invalidated by the ``index.json`` ``mtime``: it exists
        because :meth:`resolve_folders` is called for every chat save (a hot
        path) while the catalogue changes rarely.
        """
        index_file = self._index_file()
        try:
            mtime = os.path.getmtime(index_file)
        except OSError:
            mtime = None
        if self._cache is not None and self._cache_key == (index_file, mtime):
            return self._cache

        boards: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
        index = self._read_json(index_file) or {}
        for entry in index.get("boards") or []:
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            board = self._read_json(self._board_file(entry.get("id"))) or {}
            merged = {**entry, **board}
            title = str(merged.get("title") or entry.get("title") or "").strip()
            if title:
                boards[title.lower()] = merged

        self._cache_key = (index_file, mtime)
        self._cache = boards
        return boards

    def invalidate(self) -> None:
        """Drop the in-memory catalogue cache."""
        self._cache_key = None
        self._cache = None

    def load(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Load the whole catalogue in the assembled (legacy compatible) shape.

        Returns:
            ``{"version": 2, "boards": {"<title>": {...}}, "tags": {...}}``.

        Example:
            >>> KanbanStore("/proj/.codx/tasks").load()["boards"].keys()
            dict_keys(['Bugs', 'Sprint 12'])
        """
        self.migrate_if_needed()
        index = self._read_json(self._index_file())

        if index is None:
            # Not migrated and nothing to migrate: behave like an empty project.
            legacy = self._read_json(self._path(LEGACY_FILE))
            if legacy:
                logger.warning(
                    "kanban: reading the legacy file at '%s' directly (migration "
                    "did not run)",
                    self._path(LEGACY_FILE),
                )
                return self._assemble_legacy(legacy)
            return {"version": STORE_VERSION, "boards": {}, "tags": {}}

        boards: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        order: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
        for position, entry in enumerate(index.get("boards") or []):
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            board = self._read_json(self._board_file(entry.get("id"))) or {}
            merged = {**entry, **board}
            title = str(merged.get("title") or entry.get("title") or "").strip()
            if not title:
                continue
            boards[title] = merged
            order.append((int(merged.get("order") or position), title))

        # Preserve the catalogue order so the board list does not jump around.
        ordered = {
            title: boards[title] for _, title in sorted(order, key=lambda item: item[0])
        }
        return {
            "version": index.get("version") or STORE_VERSION,
            "boards": ordered,
            "tags": index.get("tags") or {},
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _assemble_legacy(legacy: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Shape a raw v1 payload like :meth:`load` does."""
        if not legacy.get("version"):
            return {
                "version": STORE_VERSION,
                "boards": legacy if isinstance(legacy.get("boards"), dict) else {},
                "tags": {},
            }
        return legacy

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Folder resolution (used by ChatManager.get_chat_file)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def resolve_folders(
        self,
        board: Optional[str],
        column: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Tuple[str, str]:
        """
        Resolve the *folders* of a board/column from their (mutable) titles.

        Because ``title`` is only a label, the storage path of a task must be
        computed from the immutable ``folder``. Two fallbacks keep old projects
        and hand‑edited catalogues working:

        1. when the folder recorded in the catalogue no longer exists on disk,
           an existing directory with the same name (case insensitive) is used,
        2. when the board is unknown, the title itself is used (v1 behaviour).

        Args:
            board: Board title (``Chat.board``).
            column: Column title (``Chat.column``).

        Returns:
            Tuple of ``(board_folder, column_folder)``.

        Example:
            >>> store.resolve_folders("Bugs", "In progress")
            ('Bugs', 'In progress')
        """
        board_title = str(board or DEFAULT_BOARD).strip() or DEFAULT_BOARD
        column_title = str(column or DEFAULT_COLUMN).strip() or DEFAULT_COLUMN

        info = self._catalogue().get(board_title.lower()) or {}
        board_folder = str(info.get("folder") or "").strip() or safe_folder(board_title, DEFAULT_BOARD)

        columns = {}
        for entry in info.get("columns") or []:
            if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("title"):
                columns[str(entry["title"]).strip().lower()] = (
                    str(entry.get("folder") or "").strip() or safe_folder(entry["title"], DEFAULT_COLUMN)
                )
            elif isinstance(entry, str):
                columns[entry.strip().lower()] = safe_folder(entry, DEFAULT_COLUMN)

        column_folder = columns.get(column_title.lower()) or safe_folder(column_title, DEFAULT_COLUMN)

        existing_board = self._existing_dir(self.tasks_path, board_folder)
        if existing_board:
            board_folder = existing_board

        board_abs_path = self._path(board_folder)
        if os.path.isdir(board_abs_path):
            existing_column = self._existing_dir(board_abs_path, column_folder)
            if existing_column:
                column_folder = existing_column

        return board_folder, column_folder

    @staticmethod
    def _existing_dir(parent_path: str, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Return the real name of *name* inside *parent_path* (case insensitive).

        Args:
            parent_path: Folder to look into.
            name: Expected directory name.

        Returns:
            The directory name as stored on disk, or None when absent.
        """
        if not name or not os.path.isdir(parent_path):
            return None
        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(parent_path, name)):
            return name
        wanted = name.strip().lower()
        try:
            for entry in os.listdir(parent_path):
                if entry.strip().lower() == wanted and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(parent_path, entry)):
                    return entry
        except OSError as ex:
            logger.warning("kanban: cannot list '%s': %s", parent_path, ex)
        return None

    def board_dirs(self) -> List[str]:
        """
        Return the folders that hold chats (every directory except ``boards``).

        Returns:
            List of folder names directly under ``tasks``.
        """
        try:
            entries = os.listdir(self.tasks_path)
        except OSError:
            return []
        return sorted(
            entry for entry in entries
            if not entry.startswith(".")
            and entry != BOARDS_DIR
            and os.path.isdir(self._path(entry))
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Writing
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _iter_boards(raw_boards: Any) -> List[Tuple[str, Dict[str, Any]]]:
        """Normalize ``kanban["boards"]`` (dict or list) into ``[(name, entry)]``."""
        if isinstance(raw_boards, dict):
            return [
                (str(name), entry if isinstance(entry, dict) else {})
                for name, entry in raw_boards.items()
            ]
        if isinstance(raw_boards, list):
            return [
                (
                    str(entry.get("title") or entry.get("name") or entry.get("id") or ""),
                    entry,
                )
                for entry in raw_boards
                if isinstance(entry, dict)
            ]
        return []

    @staticmethod
    def _find_existing(
        existing: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
        board_id: Optional[str],
        title: str,
    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Find a stored board entry by id, then by (case insensitive) title."""
        if board_id and board_id in existing:
            return existing[board_id]
        wanted = (title or "").strip().lower()
        if not wanted:
            return None
        return next(
            (
                entry for entry in existing.values()
                if str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower() == wanted
            ),
            None,
        )

    def _normalize_columns(
        self,
        columns: Any,
        previous: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Normalize a board's columns to ``[{id, title, color, folder, order}]``.

        ``id`` and ``folder`` are inherited from *previous* (matched by title)
        so a rename of a column keeps the chats where they are.

        Args:
            columns: Raw columns (list of dicts/strings or a ``{title: {...}}`` dict).
            previous: Columns currently stored for the same board.

        Returns:
            Normalized column list.
        """
        by_title = {
            str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower(): entry
            for entry in (previous or [])
            if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("title")
        }

        if isinstance(columns, dict):
            items: List[Any] = [
                {"title": name, **(value if isinstance(value, dict) else {})}
                for name, value in columns.items()
            ]
        elif isinstance(columns, list):
            items = columns
        else:
            items = []

        normalized: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for order, column in enumerate(items):
            if isinstance(column, str):
                column = {"title": column}
            if not isinstance(column, dict):
                continue
            title = str(column.get("title") or column.get("name") or "").strip()
            if not title:
                continue
            previous_column = by_title.get(title.lower()) or {}
            normalized.append({
                "id": column.get("id") or previous_column.get("id") or str(uuid.uuid4()),
                "title": title,
                "color": column.get("color") if column.get("color") is not None
                         else previous_column.get("color") or "",
                "folder": column.get("folder") or previous_column.get("folder")
                          or safe_folder(title, DEFAULT_COLUMN),
                "order": column.get("order") if column.get("order") is not None else order,
            })
        return normalized

    def _normalize_board(
        self,
        name: str,
        entry: Dict[str, Any],
        existing: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
        order: int,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Build the definition that will be written for a single board.

        Args:
            name: Key used for the board in the assembled document.
            entry: Board entry as received (may be partial).
            existing: Boards currently stored (keyed by id).
            order: Position of the board in the catalogue.

        Returns:
            The full board definition (id/folder/title/columns always present).
        """
        title = str(entry.get("title") or name or "").strip() or str(entry.get("id") or "board")
        stored = self._find_existing(existing, entry.get("id"), title) or {}

        board_type = str(entry.get("type") or stored.get("type") or BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN).strip().lower()
        folder = (
            entry.get("folder")
            or stored.get("folder")
            or safe_folder(title, DEFAULT_BOARD)
        )

        return {
            **stored,
            **entry,
            "id": entry.get("id") or stored.get("id") or str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "title": title,
            "description": entry.get("description") if entry.get("description") is not None
                           else stored.get("description") or "",
            "type": board_type or BOARD_TYPE_KANBAN,
            "parent_id": entry.get("parent_id", stored.get("parent_id")),
            "folder": folder,
            "columns": self._normalize_columns(
                columns=entry.get("columns", stored.get("columns")),
                previous=stored.get("columns"),
            ),
            "order": order,
        }

    def save(self, kanban: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """
        Persist the assembled catalogue (the shape returned by :meth:`load`).

        The document is diffed against the stored index: boards that are still
        present are rewritten (one file each), boards that disappeared are
        removed, and the index is written last so it is always consistent with
        the board files.

        Args:
            kanban: ``{"version", "boards", "tags"}``.

        Example:
            >>> store.save({"version": 2, "boards": {"Bugs": {...}}, "tags": {}})
        """
        kanban = kanban if isinstance(kanban, dict) else {}
        with self.locked():
            self.migrate_if_needed()
            self.invalidate()

            index = self._read_json(self._index_file()) or {}
            existing = {
                str(entry.get("id")): entry
                for entry in index.get("boards") or []
                if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("id")
            }

            entries: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
            written_ids = set()

            for order, (name, entry) in enumerate(self._iter_boards(kanban.get("boards"))):
                board = self._normalize_board(
                    name=name, entry=entry, existing=existing, order=order
                )
                board_id = str(board["id"])
                self._write_json(self._board_file(board_id), board)
                written_ids.add(board_id)
                entries.append({
                    "id": board_id,
                    "title": board["title"],
                    "type": board["type"],
                    "parent_id": board.get("parent_id"),
                    "folder": board["folder"],
                    "order": order,
                })

            # Remove the definitions of the boards that are no longer present.
            for board_id in set(existing) - written_ids:
                self.remove_board_files(board_id)

            self._write_json(self._index_file(), {
                "version": STORE_VERSION,
                "boards": entries,
                "tags": kanban.get("tags") or index.get("tags") or {},
            })
            self.invalidate()

        logger.info(
            "kanban: saved %d board(s) for '%s'", len(entries), self.tasks_path
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Deletion
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def remove_board_files(self, board_id: str) -> None:
        """
        Delete the definition folder of *board_id* (chats are not touched).

        Args:
            board_id: Id of the board whose definition to delete.
        """
        board_dir = self._board_dir(board_id)
        if not os.path.isdir(board_dir):
            return
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(board_dir)
        except OSError as ex:
            logger.warning("kanban: cannot remove '%s': %s", board_dir, ex)

    def remove_board(self, title: str) -> bool:
        """
        Remove a board from the catalogue (definition only).

        Args:
            title: Board title (case insensitive).

        Returns:
            True when the board existed and was removed.
        """
        wanted = str(title or "").strip().lower()
        if not wanted:
            return False

        with self.locked():
            self.invalidate()
            index = self._read_json(self._index_file()) or {}
            entries = [
                entry for entry in index.get("boards") or []
                if isinstance(entry, dict)
            ]
            kept = [
                entry for entry in entries
                if str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower() != wanted
            ]
            if len(kept) == len(entries):
                return False
            for entry in entries:
                if str(entry.get("title") or "").strip().lower() == wanted:
                    self.remove_board_files(str(entry.get("id")))
            self._write_json(self._index_file(), {
                "version": STORE_VERSION,
                "boards": kept,
                "tags": index.get("tags") or {},
            })
            self.invalidate()

        logger.info("kanban: board '%s' removed from the catalogue", title)
        return True

    @property
    def backup_file(self) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the v1 backup created by the migration."""
        return self._path(BACKUP_FILE)

The kanban catalogue (boards, sprints and columns) lives in the project's

the package is free, and a missing optional submodule only fails when the

    """
    Resolve the storage folders of a board/column without instantiating a store.

    Convenience helper for callers that only need the path of a task.

    Args:
        tasks_path: Absolute ``<codx_path>/tasks`` folder.
        board: Board title (``Chat.board``).
        column: Column title (``Chat.column``).

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(board_folder, column_folder)``.

def __getattr__(name: str) -> Any:
    """
    Resolve the public names lazily (PEP 562).

    Args:
        name: Attribute being accessed.

    Returns:
        The imported attribute.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: When the name is not part of the public API.
    """
    target = _LAZY_EXPORTS.get(name)
    if target is None:
        raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")

    from importlib import import_module

    module_name, attribute = target
    module = import_module(module_name)
    return getattr(module, name if attribute is None else attribute)

"""
Canonical task creation for codx-junior.

A **task** is a :class:`~codx.junior.db.Chat` stored in
``.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/`` (kanban). This module is the only place where
a task is built and persisted, so the creation rules are enforced once and
every entry point behaves exactly the same.

Creation rules
--------------
1. **Only two kinds of callers may create tasks**: the LLM tools
   (``create_task`` and ``project_manager(action="create_task")``) and the API
   endpoints (``POST /api/chats/tasks``). Both delegate here.
2. **All the information must come from the caller.** ``name`` and
   ``description`` are mandatory: there is no AI step that expands, splits or
   rewrites a task after creation.
3. **Nothing is inherited from the parent chat.** ``profiles``, ``files``,
   ``board``, ``column``, ``sprints``, ``tags`` and the first message come
   exclusively from the arguments. Only the *linkage* (``parent_id``) and the
   project scope are resolved from the parent chat, when one is given.
4. **Every task knows its root.** :func:`codx.junior.identity.link_parent`
   stamps ``root_id`` from the parent (``parent.root_id or parent.id``), so all
   the tasks of a tree — no matter how deep — resolve to the same main task.
   That invariant is what the long-running runner relies on to decide whether a
   task belongs to a run.

Deprecated entry points (removed by this module)
------------------------------------------------
* ``ChatEngineActions.generate_tasks`` — turned a conversation into a list of
  sub-tasks and processed each one through the engine.
* ``TaskManager.create_tasks_from_prompt`` — asked the model for a task list.

import logging
from typing import Any, List, Optional

from codx.junior.chat_manager import ChatManager
from codx.junior.db import Chat, Message
from codx.junior.identity import link_parent
from codx.junior.settings import CODXJuniorSettings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Default destination, matching ChatManager defaults.
DEFAULT_BOARD = "kanban"
DEFAULT_COLUMN = "tasks"
DEFAULT_MODE = "chat"


def to_list(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Normalize a string, iterable or None into a clean list of strings.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        List of non-empty, stripped strings (order preserved).

    Example:
        >>> to_list("ui")
        ['ui']
        >>> to_list([" ui ", "", None])
        ['ui']
    """
    if value is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(value, str):
        value = [value]
    try:
        return [str(item).strip() for item in value if item and str(item).strip()]
    except TypeError:
        return []


def to_profile_names(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Normalize a profile list: no duplicates, no leading ``@``.

    The chat engine re-emits profiles as ``@name`` mentions, so a stored
    ``@name`` (or ``@@name``) would never resolve to a profile. Only the values
    received are used — profiles are never inherited from the parent chat.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        De-duplicated profile names, order preserved.

    Example:
        >>> to_profile_names(["@backend", "backend", " ui "])
        ['backend', 'ui']
    """
    names: List[str] = []
    for name in to_list(value):
        clean = name.lstrip("@").strip()
        if clean and clean not in names:
            names.append(clean)
    return names


def to_progress(value: Any, default: int = 0) -> int:
    """
    Clamp a completion percentage into the ``0-100`` range.

    Args:
        value: Raw progress value (may be None or a string).
        default: Value returned when ``value`` is not a number.

    Returns:
        Integer percentage.
    """
    try:
        return max(0, min(100, int(value)))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default


class TaskManager:
    """
    Canonical task (kanban chat) factory for a project.

    Attributes:
        settings: Project settings, used to resolve the project scope.
        chat_manager: Persistence layer (built from ``settings`` when omitted).
        event_manager: Optional event manager used to notify the UI.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: Optional[CODXJuniorSettings] = None,
        chat_manager: Optional[ChatManager] = None,
        event_manager=None,
        session=None,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the manager.

        Args:
            settings: Project settings.
            chat_manager: Optional ChatManager; built from ``settings`` when omitted.
            event_manager: Optional event manager (only used for notifications).
            session: Optional session, kept for backward compatibility. Used to
                resolve ``settings``, ``chat_manager`` and ``event_manager`` when
                they are not provided explicitly.

        Raises:
            ValueError: When neither a chat manager nor settings are available.
        """
        self.settings = settings or getattr(session, "settings", None)
        self.event_manager = event_manager or getattr(session, "event_manager", None)

        self.chat_manager = chat_manager
        if self.chat_manager is None and session is not None:
            try:
                self.chat_manager = session.get_chat_manager()
            except (AttributeError, TypeError):
                self.chat_manager = None
        if self.chat_manager is None:
            if self.settings is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "TaskManager requires project settings or a chat manager"
                )
            self.chat_manager = ChatManager(
                settings=self.settings,
                event_manager=self.event_manager,
            )

    def create_task(
        self,
        name: str,
        description: str,
        content: Optional[str] = None,
        board: Optional[str] = None,
        column: Optional[str] = None,
        sprints: Any = None,
        status: Optional[str] = None,
        priority: Optional[str] = None,
        due_date: Optional[str] = None,
        progress: Any = 0,
        assignees: Any = None,
        profiles: Any = None,
        files: Any = None,
        tags: Any = None,
        parent_id: Optional[str] = None,
        parent_chat: Optional[Chat] = None,
        project_id: Optional[str] = None,
        owner_project_id: Optional[str] = None,
        user: Optional[str] = None,
        mode: str = DEFAULT_MODE,
    ) -> Chat:
        """
        Create and persist a task with the information provided by the caller.

        Only the arguments are used: nothing is copied from ``parent_chat`` but
        the linkage (``parent_id``) and the project scope fallbacks. The
        destination (board/column/sprint/state) is validated by the caller that
        knows the project catalogue (``project_manager``); this method only
        applies the defaults.

        The ancestor chain is kept consistent: ``root_id`` is stamped from the
        parent through :func:`codx.junior.identity.link_parent`, so a task
        created from any depth of a tree still resolves to the same main task.

        Args:
            name: Task name/title (required).
            description: Complete task description (required).
            content: First user message; defaults to ``description``.
            board: Kanban board; defaults to ``kanban``.
            column: Kanban column; defaults to ``tasks``.
            sprints: Sprint identifiers to associate (each one is a board).
            status: Initial task state (``Chat.status``).
            priority: Task priority (``high`` / ``medium`` / ``low``).
            due_date: Due date in ISO format (``YYYY-MM-DD``).
            progress: Completion percentage (clamped to 0-100).
            assignees: Assigned usernames.
            profiles: Profiles/roles for the task (parameter only).
            files: Files related to the task (parameter only).
            tags: Tags for categorizing the task.
            parent_id: Parent chat id (falls back to ``parent_chat.id``).
            parent_chat: Chat that triggered the creation (scope + linkage only).
            project_id: Project the task works on (falls back to the parent).
            owner_project_id: Project that stores the task (falls back to the parent).
            user: Author username.
            mode: Chat mode of the task (``task`` by default).

        Returns:
            The persisted :class:`~codx.junior.db.Chat`.

        Raises:
            ValueError: When ``name`` or ``description`` is missing.

        Example:
            >>> TaskManager(settings).create_task(
            ...     name="Fix login timeout",
            ...     description="## Context\nThe login times out after 30s...",
            ...     board="kanban",
            ...     column="tasks",
            ...     profiles=["backend"],
            ... )
        """
        name = (name or "").strip()
        description = (description or "").strip()

        if not name:
            raise ValueError("name is required to create a task")
        if not description:
            raise ValueError(
                "description is required to create a task: tasks are created "
                "with all their information (there is no AI sub-task "
                "generation anymore)"
            )

        settings_project_id = getattr(self.settings, "project_id", None)
        task_profiles = to_profile_names(profiles)
        task_files = to_list(files)

        task = Chat(
            name=name,
            description=description,
            parent_id=parent_id or getattr(parent_chat, "id", None),
            board=(board or DEFAULT_BOARD).strip(),
            column=(column or DEFAULT_COLUMN).strip(),
            sprints=to_list(sprints),
            status=(status or "").strip(),
            priority=priority,
            due_date=due_date,
            progress=to_progress(progress),
            assignees=to_list(assignees),
            profiles=task_profiles,
            file_list=task_files,
            tags=to_list(tags),
            project_id=(
                project_id
                or getattr(parent_chat, "project_id", None)
                or settings_project_id
            ),
            owner_project_id=(
                owner_project_id
                or getattr(parent_chat, "owner_project_id", None)
                or settings_project_id
            ),
            mode=mode,
        )

        # Ancestor invariant: parent_id (when missing) + root_id from the parent.
        # When the parent chat is not loaded, save_chat resolves and backfills
        # root_id walking parent_id.
        link_parent(chat=task, parent_chat=parent_chat)

        task.messages.append(
            Message(
                role="user",
                content=(content or description).strip(),
                profiles=task_profiles,
                files=task_files,
                user=user,
            )
        )

        saved_task = self.chat_manager.save_chat(chat=task)

        logger.info(
            "TaskManager: task created id='%s' name='%s' board='%s' column='%s' "
            "sprints=%s profiles=%s parent_id=%s root_id=%s",
            saved_task.id,
            saved_task.name,
            saved_task.board,
            saved_task.column,
            saved_task.sprints,
            task_profiles,
            saved_task.parent_id,
            saved_task.root_id,
        )

        if self.event_manager is not None:
            try:
                self.event_manager.chat_event(
                    chat=saved_task,
                    message=f"Task '{saved_task.name}' created",
                    event_type="created",
                )
            except Exception as ex:
                logger.warning("TaskManager: could not emit chat event: %s", ex)

        return saved_task

    applied against the chat file ``mtime``. When a bound is ``None`` it is
    ignored, so existing callers are unaffected.

NEW — accumulated chat cost (``Chat.cost``):
    ``Chat.cost`` accumulates the cxjcoins spent on a chat. It is updated here
    whenever a message carrying a cost is added or updated, using the persisted
    version of that message as the baseline (so a cost registered *after* the
    message was first persisted is still captured exactly once). The value is
    MONOTONIC — deleting a message never reduces it — so the chat budget stays
    accurate even when messages are removed.

NEW — cost roll-up to the root chat:
    The same delta is also added to the **root** chat of the tree
    (``Chat.root_id``, see :mod:`codx.junior.identity`). That makes the budget
    of a main task (``Chat.estimation_cost``) cover every descendant turn, which
    is what a long-running run needs: the run budget lives on the main task and
    the agent already stops a turn when ``Chat.cost`` reaches
    ``Chat.estimation_cost``.

NEW — chat status history (``Chat.status_history``):
    ``Chat.status`` was previously a single mutable field ("last writer wins"),
    making it impossible to reconstruct when a task moved between statuses. This
    module now appends a :class:`codx.junior.db.ChatStatusEvent` to
    ``Chat.status_history`` every time ``status`` actually changes (detected in
    :meth:`ChatManager.save_chat` via :meth:`ChatManager._register_status_change`).
    The log is append-only and merge-safe (dedup by ``doc_id``), giving future
    task-performance metrics (cycle time, throughput, error rate) the raw
    transition feed they need.
"""
